sections.html:
Your envelope arrives from Orange County, not from City Hall. Orlando picks its own rate, yet the county appraiser puts the number on your house, and the county Tax Collector prints one combined statement and takes the payment. The city says it keeps about 35 cents of every property tax dollar. The rest is divided among Orange County, Orange County Public Schools, the St. Johns water management district and the library system.

Questions about the amount owed go to a county office. Questions about services, permits and the city budget go to the city.

  • Orange County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, mailing address
  • Orange County Tax Collector: bills, payments, delinquent taxes, certificates
  • City of Orlando: its own millage rate and budget

Orlando's own rate is 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and the city reports it has not moved in over ten years. One mill equals a tenth of a cent per dollar of taxable value. Treat it as a single line item: the county, the school system and the water district each add their own, and special assessments sit below those.

The Property Appraiser posts the final millage for every taxing body by year. To see what a particular address pays, pull its actual bill from the Tax Collector. Neighborhoods and special taxing districts produce different totals.

The city counts about 333,888 residents, 8.4 percent more than in 2020, spread over 131,179 households. Fewer than half of those households own, and the median value of an owned home is $394,100. Roughly six in ten residents rent. Expect investors in the buyer pool, and expect that a tenant could already live in the house you are selling.

Hand any buyer the Tax Collector's account page and tell them whether an exemption is in place. If a special district line appears on your bill, point it out before the buyer's review period begins.

sections.h2: Due dates, discounts and late charges
sections.html:
Statements are mailed by the beginning of November. Full price is owed through March 31. Paying sooner earns a break of 4 percent in November that shrinks every month until it hits 1 percent in February. On April 1 anything left over turns late.

Orange County payment schedule
Pay duringResult
November4 percent discount
February1 percent discount
By March 31Gross amount, no discount
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3 percent minimum charge plus advertising cost
By June 1Certificate auction, bids opening at 18 percent

The clock runs on arrival, not postmark. A check mailed on March 31 and delivered April 3 counts as late. Homeowners with a mortgage escrow may see only a copy of the statement, so make sure the lender really sent the payment.

Think the value is too high? The countdown is 25 days, and it starts on the date printed on the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes that the appraiser mails every August. The petition is one of the DR-486 forms, and the clerk of the court receives it.

A rejected exemption has its own window of 30 days after the denial letter goes out, and that petition is directed to the value adjustment board. Public hearings by the taxing bodies fill September and October, and the final statements follow in November.

  • Open the August notice as soon as it comes.
  • Count from the mailing date printed on the notice itself.
  • Phone the appraiser before you file, since plenty of mistakes get corrected informally.

Put the notice in your sale folder. It shows a buyer what the county proposes before final rates are set.

sections.h2: Homestead, Save Our Homes and portability
sections.html:
A homestead exemption takes as much as $50,000 off the value that gets taxed. A second rule, Save Our Homes, puts a lid on how quickly the assessment of a homestead can rise: the lower of 3 percent or inflation. The Department of Revenue's chart lists the lid as 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024.

The lid and the savings it built are tied to you rather than to the property. Once the deed changes hands, full just value applies from the next January 1, so the buyer's opening bill can land well above what you paid. Staying in Florida? Portability lets part of the accumulated savings follow you. It is claimed on the exemption application for the new home, due March 1, and you must be within three years of leaving the old homestead.

Ask the county Tax Collector for a payoff figure in writing. The closing agent will subtract any late balance from your proceeds. Used the homestead tax deferral in the past? Ask the Tax Collector how that deferred amount is repaid when the house sells.

  • Check the parcel for a sold tax certificate.
  • Once April 1 has gone by, plan to pay with certified or cashier's funds, a money order or cash in person.
  • A certificate left unredeemed for two years is urgent, because a tax deed application can come next.
  • Ask the lender's escrow department whether this year's bill has been paid.

One reason owners with a lien consider a direct cash sale is that it skips lender underwriting and appraisal delays and can close fast. Compare that against agent fees, repairs and the time a regular listing needs.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call the offices
sections.html:
A short call goes faster with details in hand. Have the parcel ID or the street address, the name exactly as it appears on the deed, and the most recent statement. Write down the name of the person you spoke with and the date, then ask for anything you are quoted in writing. A payoff that exists only as a phone memory is hard to hand to a title company.

If you are weighing a standard listing against a quick cash sale, ask the same questions either way. The tax picture on the parcel does not change with the sale route, and a clean payoff figure makes both options simpler.

sections.h2: A simple checklist before you list
sections.html:
Do these in order. Look up the parcel at the Property Appraiser and check that the owner names and exemptions are right. Then open the Tax Collector's account page and write down which years show paid. If a balance is open, ask for the payoff letter. Last, collect your most recent statement and the August notice so the title agent has them.

Also decide how the current year will be split with the buyer and say so to your closing agent. November bills and year-round closings do not line up, so the contract should spell out who covers the months each side owned the home.

faqs.q: Does Orlando collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Orange County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city's levy. Orlando sets its own millage rate and keeps about 35 cents of each dollar.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate in Orlando?
faqs.a: The city's rate is 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and it has held for more than ten years. Your bill also carries county, school and district levies.

faqs.q: When do Orlando property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The full amount is due by March 31, and payment must reach the Tax Collector by then. A 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost follow.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap carry over when I sell in Orlando?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, filed by March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I check my tax bill before listing a house in Orlando?
faqs.a: Search the Orange County Tax Collector's records by owner name, parcel ID or address. The Property Appraiser's parcel record shows value and exemptions.
